minor.issue: No delete endpoint exists (405 Method Not Allowed). Testing agents and admins cannot clean up apps created by live-sync — synced test apps (e.g. 'Spotify: Music & Podcasts') now pollute super_admin's applications list. Consider adding an admin-only DELETE endpoint.

issues: Radix DialogContent console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for {DialogContent}'. Same a11y warning family as iter_1's ReviewDialog. Add DialogDescription or aria-describedby. Non-blocking.

The GooglePlaySync trigger renders twice on the page (once inside PageHeader actions, once inside the gplay-live-card). Both share data-testid='gplay-sync-btn'. Not harmful but yields duplicate testids — Playwright must use .first. Consider giving the header CTA a distinct testid.

action_items: (minor) Add DialogDescription/aria-describedby to GooglePlaySync's DialogContent to silence Radix a11y warning.
(minor) Give the header 'Live Sync (Google Play)' trigger a distinct data-testid (e.g. gplay-sync-btn-header) so testids remain unique.

(minor) Provide an admin-only DELETE /api/applications/{id} endpoint (with cascading delete of its reviews/snapshots/sync_jobs) so live-synced test apps can be cleaned. Current run left 'Spotify: Music and Podcasts' + 'Spotify: Music & Podcasts' in super_admin org.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_gplay.sync: for non-super_admin, existing-app lookup filters by organization_id; for super_admin it uses global lookup {'package_id': package_id}. Under a super_admin two different client orgs could not each own the same package_id — the first hit (any org) is returned. Fine for now (super_admin is a single global operator), but worth documenting.

gplay.fetch_reviews: uses google_play_scraper's continuation_token loop with a max_count cap of 600. No retry/backoff on transient network errors — a single flaky HTTP causes 502. Consider a light retry (2-3x with backoff) inside fetch_reviews since it runs in a thread anyway.

gplay endpoint is fully synchronous (asyncio.to_thread). Fetching 200+ reviews over slow Play endpoints can exceed the ingress ~100s cutoff and produce user-visible 502 even though the DB inserts succeeded. Consider (a) reducing default max_count from 200 to 100, or (b) offloading to a background job + status endpoint.

routes_gplay: rating_snapshots upsert uses reviews=len(fetched) (all fetched, not net imported) — if a manager syncs twice a day the snapshot's 'reviews' counter double-counts duplicates. Consider len(to_insert) instead of len(fetched).

Frontend GooglePlaySync.jsx: 'max' input min=10 max=600 but backend has no upper enforcement beyond min(max_count or 200, 600) inside gplay.fetch_reviews. Good defense-in-depth; add server-side pydantic constraint (e.g. Field(le=600, ge=1)) for clarity.

Duplicate GooglePlaySync <Button/> rendered on Integrations page — two DOM nodes carry the same data-testid='gplay-sync-btn' (header actions + live card). Only visual issue but breaks testid uniqueness.
